$comment: The host-port allocation record. Every local development stack publishes
its host ports from a dedicated block of 20, so any combination of stacks
runs at once without colliding. standards/016-local-development.md carries
the rules; this file carries the allocation, because an allocation is the
one thing a rule cannot derive.
IT IS NOT A ROSTER OF WHO IS SUBJECT TO THE STANDARD, and the distinction
matters. dependency-versions.json states the reason it keeps no such list:
a repository opts in by calling job-ci-conformance, the checker is handed
one clone at a time, and a handed-over client repository vendors the
standard and keeps using it after nothing in this tree can see it. All of
that still holds. A block allocation is a different kind of fact. It is a
shared namespace, like an IANA registry: absence here means unallocated,
never unbound by the rules.
SO NO PER-REPOSITORY GATE READS THIS FILE. The gate a repository runs asks
only what one clone can answer: do this stack's host bindings all fall
inside a single 20-wide window aligned to a multiple of 20, and is none of
them privileged. A repository that never appears here still passes, which
is what keeps a handed-over repository working. This file is read by one
check in this repository alone, which asserts that no two blocks overlap,
and by a person choosing a base for a new project.
CHOOSING A BASE. Dial the project's first two letters on a phone keypad and
append 00, then take the next free multiple of 20 if that base is taken.
2=ABC 3=DEF 4=GHI 5=JKL 6=MNO 7=PQRS 8=TUV 9=WXYZ. The derivation is a
starting point rather than a law, and the entries below are not all
reachable from it: some were dialled from a name's initials instead of its
first two letters. Both readings are recorded here rather than reconciled,
because a base that moves invalidates every URL anyone has typed.
Check a candidate against /etc/services before settling on it.
$blocks_comment: Project to block base. The block runs base through base+19 inclusive.
Offsets within a block are fixed by the standard, not by this file.
